pointers.sentence: `Library` holds two dictionaries, `Library.tags` and `Library.filters`, and its methods are ways of filling them (`django/template/library.py:Library`).

A module becomes a library by keeping one in a variable named `"register"`, the one name Django looks for: `import_library` imports a dotted path and returns the module's `"register"`, and raises `InvalidTemplateLibrary` when the import raises an `ImportError` or the variable is missing (`django/template/library.py:import_library`).
`Library.tag` registers a compile function as it is, under the name it is given or the function's own (`django/template/library.py:Library.tag`).

It sets each twice, on the function registered and on the innermost function under its decorators, and the comment there says why: a decorator such as `stringfilter`, which turns a filter's first argument into a string, reads the flag from the innermost function (`django/template/library.py:Library.filter`, `django/template/defaultfilters.py:stringfilter`).

It sets each twice, on the function registered and on the innermost function under its decorators, and the comment there says why: a decorator such as `stringfilter`, which turns a filter's first argument into a string, reads the flag from the innermost function (`django/template/library.py:Library.filter`, `django/template/defaultfilters.py:stringfilter`).
`DjangoTemplates.__init__` gathers the libraries before it makes its `Engine` (`django/template/backends/django.py:DjangoTemplates.__init__`).

In each package it imports every module, subpackages included, and keeps those with a `"register"`; a module that cannot be imported stops the backend from being made, an import error raised again as `InvalidTemplateLibrary` (`django/template/backends/django.py:get_package_libraries`).

A library's name is its module's path after the package: `"fleet_tags"` for the module above, `"charts.maps"` for a module in a subpackage (`django/template/backends/django.py:get_template_tag_modules`).

`get_installed_libraries` makes a dictionary of the names and paths, and `DjangoTemplates.get_templatetag_libraries` updates it with the `"libraries"` option, so a name given there replaces an installed module's (`django/template/backends/django.py:DjangoTemplates.get_templatetag_libraries`).

The dictionary is built in the order of `INSTALLED_APPS` and a later entry replaces an earlier one, so `{% load %}` finds the library of the application listed last, where of two templates of one name the first application's is found (`django/template/backends/django.py:get_installed_libraries`).

`Engine.__init__` then imports them all, whether a template ever loads them or not: `Engine.template_libraries` maps each name to its `Library`, and `Engine.template_builtins` lists the three of `Engine.default_builtins` and then those of the `"builtins"` option (`django/template/engine.py:Engine.__init__`).

It copies each builtin into its tables at once, in order, with `Parser.add_library`, a dictionary update, so a later library replaces an earlier one's tag or filter of the same name; the others it keeps by name, as `Parser.libraries` (`django/template/base.py:Parser.__init__`, `django/template/base.py:Parser.add_library`).

It copies each builtin into its tables at once, in order, with `Parser.add_library`, a dictionary update, so a later library replaces an earlier one's tag or filter of the same name; the others it keeps by name, as `Parser.libraries` (`django/template/base.py:Parser.__init__`, `django/template/base.py:Parser.add_library`).
`{% load %}` does all its work in its compile function, `load` (`django/template/defaulttags.py:load`).

It splits the tag on white space, so the names in it are words, never variables, looks each up with `find_library`, and hands the library to `Parser.add_library`; an unknown name is a `TemplateSyntaxError` that lists every name the engine knows (`django/template/defaulttags.py:find_library`).
In the form `{% load berth knots from fleet_tags %}`, `load_from_library` first builds a new `Library` of only the tags and filters named (`django/template/defaulttags.py:load_from_library`).

`simple_tag`, `simple_block_tag` and `inclusion_tag` write both for a function that only computes something, and return the function unchanged, so Python can still call it (`django/template/library.py:Library.simple_tag`).

When a template is compiled, that compile function splits the token, takes off a final `"as"` and a name where the tag allows one, and matches the rest against the signature with `parse_bits` (`django/template/library.py:parse_bits`).

When the template renders, the node resolves each argument in the context and calls the function, with the context itself first under `takes_context=True` (`django/template/library.py:TagHelperNode.get_resolved_arguments`).

With `"as"` and a name, the value is set, unescaped, in the context's top dictionary, and the tag renders the empty string (`django/template/library.py:SimpleNode.render`); set inside `{% for %}`, it is gone after `{% endfor %}`.

The compile function parses the body up to the end tag, `{% endnotice %}` for `{% notice %}` unless `end_name=` names another, and keeps its nodes (`django/template/library.py:Library.simple_block_tag`).

At each render the body is rendered in the same context and passed as the content; the rest is `SimpleNode.render`, escaping included (`django/template/library.py:SimpleBlockNode.get_resolved_arguments`).
`inclusion_tag` takes a template as well as the function, which returns a dictionary for it (`django/template/library.py:Library.inclusion_tag`).

`InclusionNode.render` calls the function, fetches a template given by name or by a list of names from the engine of the template being rendered, and keeps it in the render context under the node, so that inside `{% for %}` it is fetched once for each render of the template around it, not once a turn (`django/template/library.py:InclusionNode.render`).
